claims.claim: 50 users and a few requests a minute is well within what Flask handles. Performance is not a reason to choose anything else.
claims.measured: python-flask: 1,732 req/s plaintext, 1,700 req/s JSON and 1,529 req/s single-row DB on 1 CPU
claims.why: Flask handled more than a thousand requests per second, which is thousands of times more than a few requests a minute.

claims.claim: A Flask app plus discord.py with SQLite usually uses somewhere around 50–150 MB
claims.measured: python-flask: 115 MB idle and 117–123 MB peak; python-flask-gthread: 52 MB idle and 55–57 MB peak
claims.why: The measured Flask variants fall inside the 50–150 MB range; discord.py's extra memory wasn't measured but is unlikely to change that by more than a factor of 2.

claims.measured: python-flask: 123 MB highest peak across all tests
claims.why: The highest measured peak is about a quarter of the 512 MB limit.

claims.measured: go-gin: 2 MB idle and 8–16 MB peak; go-nethttp: 2 MB idle and 7–15 MB peak
claims.why: Both Go servers are among the lowest memory users measured, far below Python, Node and the JVM.
